policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'say all manner of evil against you falsely' with no noun for the thing said; the RP addition of ῥῆμα ('every evil word/saying') has no counterpart in the English, which renders only the substantivized πᾶν πονηρόν.

ASV 'but to be cast out and trodden under foot of men' joins the two ideas with 'and' in idiomatic English, which serves the base participle βληθὲν ἔξω governing καταπατεῖσθαι just as readily as RP's coordinated infinitives βληθῆναι ἔξω καί; the English does not expose the participle/infinitive distinction and no note is mapped here.
Word order only: ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη and ἡ δικαιοσύνη ὑμῶν both yield ASV 'your righteousness'. English possessive placement is fixed and cannot register the Greek order.

ASV text reads 'every one who is angry with his brother' with no qualifier, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities insert without cause' explicitly places εἰκῆ outside the ASV text as another authorities' insertion.
Word order only: μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ and ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ both give ASV 'while thou art with him in the way'. The verse's textual note concerns 'deliver thee', a different unit.

ASV renders a second finite clause, 'and the judge deliver thee to the officer', where the base leaves καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ verbless; the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit deliver thee' confirms σε παραδῷ stands in the ASV text and is what other authorities lack.

ASV 'and not thy whole body go into hell' renders the intransitive ἀπέλθῃ ('go'); RP's βληθῇ would require a passive 'be cast into hell', which the ASV does not have — and does use, as 'cast it from thee', earlier in the same verse for βάλε.

The RP addition is ὅτι recitativum introducing direct speech, which English renders with the comma and capital of 'It was said also, Whosoever...'; its presence or absence leaves the ASV wording identical.

ASV 'every one that putteth away his wife' renders the articular participle πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων; RP's indefinite relative ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ would give 'whosoever shall put away', the very wording the ASV uses later in this verse for ὃς ἐὰν ... γαμήσῃ ('whosoever shall marry').

ASV 'maketh her an adulteress' renders the passive μοιχευθῆναι (she is made to suffer adultery); RP's middle μοιχᾶσθαι would give 'causeth her to commit adultery', an active offence by the woman that the ASV wording excludes.
Word order only: ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν and ἢ μέλαιναν ποιῆσαι both yield ASV 'make one hair white or black'. English verb placement cannot register the Greek order.

ASV 'whosoever smiteth thee on thy right cheek' uses the simple present, matching the present indicative ῥαπίζει; the ASV marks futures with 'shall' in this very context ('Whosoever shall say', v. 22; 'Whosoever shall put away', v. 31), so RP's future ῥαπίσει would have produced 'shall smite'.

εἰς and ἐπί with σιαγόνα are both rendered 'on thy right cheek'; English has one preposition for the struck surface and the mapped note is an alternative_rendering about 'evil', which cannot decide a reading.

ASV 'thy right cheek' is equally the rendering of the bare article τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, which English regularly turns into a possessive for body parts, and of σιαγόνα σου; the possessive does not prove the pronoun stood in the Greek.
Aorist δός and present δίδου are both rendered by the English imperative 'Give'; the ASV has no iterative marker ('keep giving', 'give continually') that would distinguish the aspects.

ASV goes straight from 'Love your enemies' to 'and pray for them that persecute you', with nothing answering RP's εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς ('bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you').
ASV names only one class in the prayer clause, 'them that persecute you'; RP's ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς καί ('them that despitefully use you, and') is absent from the English.
The variant is the presence of the article in ἐν οὐρανοῖς / ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς; both are rendered 'in heaven' and the ASV shows no article for heaven in English.
ASV 'do not even the publicans the same?' renders the accusative object τὸ αὐτό; Treg's adverbial οὕτως would give 'so' or 'thus', not the noun phrase 'the same'.
ASV 'if ye salute your brethren only' renders ἀδελφούς; RP's φίλους would give 'friends'.
ASV 'do not even the Gentiles the same?' renders ἐθνικοί; RP's τελῶναι would give 'publicans', the word the ASV does use in v. 46 for τελῶναι.
ASV 'do not even the Gentiles the same?' renders the object τὸ αὐτό; RP's adverbial οὕτως would give 'so' or 'thus' rather than 'the same'.
ὡς and its strengthened form ὥσπερ are both rendered by ASV 'as'; English has no separate word for the intensified comparative particle here.

ASV 'your heavenly Father' renders the adjective οὐράνιος attributively; RP's prepositional ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς would give 'your Father who is in heaven', the phrasing the ASV uses for that construction in v. 45.
